THE OPERATING PRINCIPLE
NOTE 001 / WHY I BUILD
I don't want to collect technologies. I want to make difficult things feel simple for the person on the other side of the screen.
↗Useful beats impressive

A real workflow, a clear outcome, and fewer reasons for a user to ask “now what?”

⌘Systems need empathy

Performance, permissions, privacy, accessibility, and the details people notice when something breaks.

✳Delight is engineering too

A considered interaction can turn a functional tool into a product people remember.

THE SHAPE OF MY WORK

Four lenses.
One builder.

I like working across boundaries. The useful part is not knowing a little of everything, but connecting the right pieces to make something work end to end.

01 / SYSTEMS⌘

Make the foundations reliable.

I work on APIs, validation, database-backed workflows, authentication, role-based access, logging, and deployment. I pay attention to the parts users rarely see until they fail.

REST APIsAuth + RBACData modellingDeployment
02 / INTELLIGENCE◉

Turn signals into useful decisions.

My applied AI work spans computer vision, NLP extraction, embeddings, transfer learning, and privacy-aware on-device inference. I care about what the output means for the person using it.

Computer visionNLP / NERModel evaluationEdge inference
03 / EXPERIENCE✳

Make the next step obvious.

I build interfaces with clear states, purposeful feedback, responsive layouts, and interactions that earn their place. A feature is not finished just because it renders.

React / Next.jsResponsive UIInteraction designAccessibility mindset
04 / DELIVERY↗

Carry ideas past the demo.

I enjoy connecting implementation with practical constraints: performance, maintainability, edge cases, release workflows, and evidence that the solution actually helps.

Testing mindsetLinuxDockerGit + collaboration

A DIFFERENT KIND OF SHIP DATE → PUBLISHED
🎭

Jazbaat · Stage and street play

Core member of the IIITDMJ dramatics society. Second runner-up at BITS Hyderabad Pearl 2025 and IIT-G Alcheringa 2026. Live audiences teach timing, teamwork, and how to recover when the script meets reality.

Reading a room is useful on stage and in product design. You learn to notice when people are confused, disengaged, or ready for the next beat.
🗾

Japan is a direction, not decoration

I'm learning Japanese at beginner level and exploring opportunities with Japanese companies. I want to understand the people and culture behind the products, not just add Japanese text to a page.

This portfolio includes a Japanese-language mode as a small demonstration of intentional localisation. It is not a claim of Japanese fluency or JLPT certification.
✎

Design-minded by default

I enjoy building interfaces where visual decisions and functional decisions support each other. Good UI should feel clear, expressive, and useful without making the user work to understand it.

If an interaction has no purpose, it is decoration. If it has purpose but no feedback, it is unfinished. If it is useful and delightful, now we're talking.
